html:
Ulugh Beg was a grandson of Timur who ruled Samarkand for some forty years and was one of the great astronomers of the Middle Ages.

His father Shah Rukh, Timur's son and heir, made him governor of Samarkand when he was a teenager. He built a madrasa on the Registan square, where astronomy and mathematics were taught, and invited scholars such as the mathematician Jamshid al-Kashi.

In the 1420s he built a great observatory on a hill outside the city, described under Ulugh Beg's observatory.

  • His star catalogue of 1437, the Ulugh Beg star catalogue, gave the positions of about a thousand stars, the first major catalogue since Ptolemy.
  • He measured the length of the year to within about a minute of the modern value.

When his father died in 1447 he took the throne of the Timurid Empire, but he was a poor ruler and general. His own son rebelled, and Ulugh Beg was killed in 1449. The observatory was wrecked soon after. He is buried in the Gur-e-Amir.
sum: Ulugh Beg was a grandson of Timur who ruled Samarkand for some forty years and was one of the great astronomers of the Middle Ages.
